title: Appeal Kits for Musicians Wrongly Flagged as AI
one_liner: A DAW-side watcher that quietly notarizes your project history, so a wrongful 'AI' flag becomes a one-click appeal instead of a lost royalty stream.
customer: Independent producers and singer-songwriters releasing 5-50 tracks a year on TIDAL, Deezer, Spotify and Bandcamp, plus small labels and distributor support desks that have to rule on flagged tracks.
problem: Platforms now punish fully-AI tracks: TIDAL demonetizes them (Jul 15, 2026), Spotify excludes AI-persona profiles from recommendations (Aug 11), and Bandcamp banned AI music outright (Jan 14). Detectors are probabilistic, and with AI above 50% of Deezer uploads, thresholds will tighten and false positives will grow (my inference). A wrongly flagged human has no evidence and no appeal format. The free verified-artist badges do nothing for someone already flagged.
solution: A background agent for Ableton, Logic, Reaper and FL Studio (Ableton .als files are gzipped XML, so they diff cleanly) that hashes project files, stems, plugin chains and automation over time. It anchors the hashes to a public timestamp log and renders a shareable 'Session Timeline' page. One click exports an appeal packet formatted for each platform's dispute flow, with a verify link that distributors can check. Artists choose what to reveal and never upload raw sessions.
why_now: Enforcement went live in a six-month burst (Bandcamp Jan 2026, TIDAL Jul 15, Spotify Aug 11), so 'flagged as AI' now costs money and reach rather than a label. Detection is increasingly automated and at volume. Nobody has built the defendant's side of the process.
revenue_model: $9/month artist plan, $49 per notarized appeal packet for non-subscribers, $500-2,000/month label plans, and a per-verification API fee from distributors that want to clear flagged-track disputes faster.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody pays for proof-of-human in advance, because the badge is free. They pay at the moment of dispute. Sell the evidence, like a dashcam that is only valued after the crash, and not the badge.
first_30_days: Weeks 1-2: build a project-file watcher for Ableton and Reaper with a hosted timeline page. Weeks 3-4: recruit 30 producers from r/WeAreTheMusicMakers and producer Discords, and DM artists who have posted about false AI flags. Offer a free install and charge only for the first appeal packet. Pitch two distributor support leads on accepting the verify link.

title: Contingency Audit of Unbilled Plumbing Materials
one_liner: Reconcile a trade shop's supply-house invoices against its customer invoices and catch both parts that were bought but never billed and quiet supplier price drift, paid a percentage of what gets recovered.
customer: Plumbing, HVAC and electrical shops doing $1.5-15M in revenue with 5-40 techs, running ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro or Jobber plus QuickBooks, buying on account from Ferguson, Hajoca, Winsupply or a local supply house.
problem: Shops lose margin in two places nobody watches. First, parts go out on a supply-house ticket with a job name, or come off the truck stock, and never make it onto the customer invoice. Techs charge the labor from the flat-rate book and forget the $6 valve, the wax ring, the supply lines, the $40 of fittings. In the shops I know, when the office finally reconciles a quarter it is typically a few percent of revenue. Second, supply houses price off list with a contractor multiplier, and list prices have moved several times since the Section 232 copper, steel and aluminum tariffs (50%, working through a long manufacturer-to-contractor lag). Surcharges appear, job-quoted prices are not honored, returns credits are never issued, and no owner has time to read 40 invoices a week.
solution: Shops set up an email forwarding rule for supply-house invoices and statements and give us read access to their field-service software export. An LLM-based line-item parser ties supply-house lines to jobs and POs, then produces a weekly leak list for the office manager: (1) purchased-not-billed by job, (2) price versus the shop's own multiplier and versus the same SKU 30 days ago, (3) unclaimed return credits, (4) pricebook items where cost has risen past the target markup, with a repricing file ready to import. Later add a benchmark ('you pay 9% more than shops your size for PEX-A fittings') built from pooled anonymized invoices, which is the moat.
why_now: Tariff-driven price volatility means flat-rate pricebooks are stale within a quarter, and owners know it. Invoice parsing with LLMs went from a custom-ML project to an afternoon. Field-service platforms expose APIs and exports. The trades are also ahead of everyone else in adopting software but behind in auditing it, so there is no incumbent audit product.
revenue_model: Contingency fee of 25% of recovered and newly captured revenue for the first 12 months (no recovery, no fee), converting to a $199-499 per month subscription for continuous monitoring plus the pricing benchmark. Data licensing of the pooled price index to distributors and manufacturers later.
non_obvious_insight: Owners obsess over lead cost and tech hiring while the highest-ROI dollar is sitting in the shoebox of paid invoices. Everything a tech installs was bought on a ticket with a job name on it, so the truth is already in two systems that have never been compared. This is the freight-audit and telecom-audit model, and no one has brought it to the trades because the people who feel the pain are too busy running trucks to build it.
first_30_days: Offer a free 90-day audit to 10 shop owners from a peer group (a PHCC chapter, Nexstar or Service Roundtable style mastermind). Have them forward statements and give a one-time export. Turn each audit around in 48 hours with a single 'found money' number and a list of specific invoices. Convert the shops with the largest number to the contingency contract. A spreadsheet plus an LLM parsing script is enough for the first ten.

title: Cross-Lender Double-Pledge Registry for Receivables
one_liner: A hashed, shared ledger where lenders confirm that an invoice, receivable or auto loan has not already been pledged elsewhere, starting with freight and trade factoring.
customer: Independent factoring companies, ABL desks at regional banks, supply-chain-finance funds and private-credit lenders to mid-market suppliers.
problem: First Brands allegedly double- and triple-pledged about $2.3B of invoices. The SEC charged Tricolor's former CEO and CFO on 18 Aug 2026 with double-pledging subprime auto loans to multiple lenders and securitisations. No single funder can detect overlap because there is no mechanism for lenders to see each other's pledges, so small factors are hit constantly.
solution: Members submit hashed invoice fingerprints (debtor ID, invoice number, amount, date) by API and get 'clean' or 'conflict' back in seconds. Add automated debtor confirmation (email, portal and EDI checks that the invoice exists and where payment is directed) and remittance-diversion alerts. Use private set intersection or salted hashes so lenders never reveal borrowers, and a consortium contract plus UCC-style notice.
why_now: First Brands and Tricolor collapsed in Sept 2025, and DOJ (Jan 2026) and SEC (Aug 2026) actions followed. Private credit's growth, investor demands for collateral verification and bar-association guidance on being 'two-timed' have created board-level urgency.
revenue_model: $0.10-2 per query, $1-5k per month membership for small factors, $50k+ per year for funds, and $5-15 per automated debtor confirmation.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud lives in the gaps between lenders, not inside them. The data everyone needs (each other's pledges) is data nobody will share bilaterally. A neutral registry sells a network effect for detection, like Carfax or the UK's Cifas, rather than a better anomaly detector.
first_30_days: Start with freight factoring, where duplicate invoices and fake brokers are a known problem. Sign 10 independent factors and two fintech ABL lenders through industry associations, build the hashing API, and offer founding members a free tier in exchange for contributing data.

title: Robot Pilot Guild for Gaming-Native Gen Z
one_liner: A guild that recruits, trains and certifies gamers aged 16-25 to remotely pilot delivery robots and humanoids, with a portable verified flight-hour logbook that becomes their credential.
customer: Robotics and physical-AI companies (sidewalk delivery, warehouse, humanoid pilots) that buy validated pilot-hours and demonstration data. Workforce boards and trainees pay for certification.
problem: Robots in 2026 run on human backup: remote assistance for stuck delivery robots and teleoperated demonstrations to train humanoids. Companies staff this ad hoc through BPOs and labeling vendors, with high churn, uneven quality and no career ladder. US lab teleoperator roles are already posting at $30-$55 per hour. Gen Alpha and Gen Z raised on controllers have the reflexes but no legitimate on-ramp.
solution: Regional 'pilot houses' with standardized rigs plus at-home certification. A tiered license runs from Level 1 sidewalk assist to Level 3 dexterous manipulation, tested in simulation and on real robots. The guild is the W-2 employer of record, sells SLA-bound pilot capacity by the validated hour, and records verified hours in a portable logbook like aviation. Quality is managed through replay review and per-task acceptance rates.
why_now: Teleoperation sits at the center of humanoid and home-robot programs in 2026 (home humanoids such as 1X NEO ship with remote operators), and demonstration data is being bought like compute. Entry-level white-collar hiring is weak, so young people want alternative on-ramps. Robot companies need reliable operator supply now, not in 2030.
revenue_model: $25-$45 per validated pilot-hour billed to robot companies, targeting about 40% gross margin. Certification fees of $200-$600 paid by trainees, workforce funds or employers, plus placement fees when companies hire pilots directly.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset in physical AI is consistent, high-quality human motor demonstration, and Gen Alpha has been practicing exactly that skill for a decade. A verified flight-hour logbook turns play into a portable credential. That makes workers stickier and quality auditable, so this is a licensed guild employer rather than a gig marketplace.
first_30_days: Approach three sidewalk-delivery or warehouse-robot startups with visible remote-assist queues. Offer a paid 4-week pilot with 10 trained gamers recruited from Discord communities and community-college esports programs. Train them on the customer's own simulator and bill per validated hour. Goal: one signed pilot and one letter of intent for a 50-pilot cohort.

title: Virtual Detention Basin from Smart Cisterns
one_liner: Thousands of backyard tanks that pre-drain before forecast storms, coordinated like a virtual power plant for stormwater.
customer: Stormwater utilities and sewer districts under combined-sewer consent decrees, and cities running basement-flooding programs.
problem: Utilities spend billions on tunnels and tanks to control overflows and basement flooding, while private-lot storage sits unmanaged because each barrel is dumb. FEMA money is unstable, so cities want cheaper capacity.
solution: Forecast-controlled cisterns and rain gardens with low-cost cellular valves that pre-drain ahead of storms and hold water at the peak, driven by AI weather ensemble forecasts. The utility pays per managed gallon at peak. First product is a 200-tank pilot in one sewershed, retrofitting existing barrels with a roughly $150 controller.
why_now: AI weather ensembles (operational since 2025) make per-storm control affordable, cellular valves are cheap, and consent-decree deadlines and unstable FEMA funding push cities toward distributed capacity.
revenue_model: Per managed gallon or per tank-year utility contracts, plus grants and rebates covering hardware.
non_obvious_insight: A city's cheapest new detention basin is 10,000 backyards coordinated like a virtual power plant.
first_30_days: Identify 3 combined-sewer cities with rebate programs, retrofit 50 existing barrels with controllers, and measure peak outflow reduction.

title: Paid Shelter-Dog Field Trips, Fees Per Adoption
one_liner: Professional walkers take the longest-stay shelter dogs on 3-hour public field trips with photos and behavior reports, and shelters pay a small trip fee plus a success fee for each adoption.
customer: Municipal and county shelters and large humane societies (paying for outcomes), with pet-food brands, pet insurers, and community foundations as sponsors.
problem: Big adult dogs, especially bully-breed types, sit in kennels for months. Kennel stress makes them look their worst: barking, spinning, lunging. Adopters decide in about 30 seconds. Volunteers do field trips but are untrained for the hard dogs, unreliable, and unscalable. Every extra day in the kennel costs the shelter real money and raises the odds of a bad outcome.
solution: A walker collects the dog for a 3-hour outing in an 'Adopt Me' vest along a cafe, park, and errand route. They shoot 10 standardized photos and video, and file a behavior report (leash manners, other dogs, cats, car ride, house-training, energy). That content goes onto the shelter's listing and a hyperlocal 'Dog of the Week' list pushed through the walker's client network. Adopted dogs get a paid 7-day decompression check-in that also reduces returns. Everything is tracked against matched dogs to prove the effect on length of stay.
why_now: Shelters have been running over capacity for the past few years, with intake outpacing adoption and large dogs backing up, and budgets are tight. Housing and landlord pet restrictions keep driving relinquishments. Funders and municipalities increasingly want outcome-based spending, and walkers now have the cheap phone video and social distribution to make a dog look like a dog and not like a kennel number. I could not re-verify current national shelter statistics in this session, so quote local data in the pitch.
revenue_model: About $35 to $50 per field trip paid by the shelter or a sponsor, plus a $150 to $300 success fee per adoption within 30 days. Benchmark the success fee against the shelter's own cost per kennel day. Optional sponsored 'field trip' slots from pet brands and insurers, and grant funding to seed the first shelter.
non_obvious_insight: A dog is evaluated in the worst possible environment, and the fix is not better marketing, it is moving the evaluation out of the kennel. Professional walkers have exactly what volunteers lack: leash skill with hard dogs, idle midday capacity, and a trusted network of 50 to 100 households that will actually meet a dog because the walker they trust is holding the leash.
first_30_days: Offer the shelter's volunteer or foster coordinator a free pilot on the 10 longest-stay dogs, with two or three of your own walkers. Track days-to-adoption against similar dogs not taken out. After 30 days, hand the director a one-page results sheet and ask for a paid pilot, or apply for a local pet-industry or community foundation grant to fund the first 100 trips.

title: Flight Recorder for AI-Drafted Police Reports
one_liner: Vendor-agnostic middleware that captures the AI draft, every officer edit and timestamp, then issues a court-ready authorship record, the process-based 'human-made' proof creators lack, so prosecutors will accept AI-assisted reports.
customer: Police departments and sheriffs' offices ($60-150 per officer per year), city and county attorneys and DA offices that must vouch for reports, and public defender offices (per-case discovery audits).
problem: Tools such as Axon's Draft One write narratives from body-cam audio, and reporting in 2025 said original AI drafts are not retained (prior knowledge). California SB 524 (effective 2026) requires disclosure of AI use and retention of first drafts, Utah requires disclaimers, and King County prosecutors said in 2024 they would reject AI-assisted reports (prior knowledge). Defense has the same failure mode: a SOCOM analyst's chatbot fabricated a ship's cargo manifest that was formatted as an official intelligence summary, with no provenance layer in the workflow.
solution: A capture layer inside the report editor or records-management system logs the body-cam transcript hash, the AI draft, each officer edit as a diff, and time-on-task, with per-paragraph officer attestations ('I observed' or 'I reviewed'). It emits a signed content-credential-style record attached to the report, a redacted discovery packet for defense, and a DA-portal view that applies each office's acceptance rules.
why_now: State laws requiring disclosure and draft retention are in force in 2026. AI report-writing is spreading while DA acceptance remains the gate. Process-based provenance standards (C2PA) now exist, and GenAI.mil's 2M-user rollout shows the same official-looking-AI-text problem is arriving federally.
revenue_model: Per-officer SaaS, per-case discovery-packet fees to public defenders, and later federal licenses for labeling AI-assisted analytic products.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck to AI report-writing is admissibility and credibility, not accuracy, and the real gatekeepers are DAs, not police chiefs. A DA who publishes an acceptance standard requiring a verifiable authorship record forces every vendor to comply, so give the standard to DAs first and sell the ledger to departments second.
first_30_days: Get one DA's office in a state with an SB 524-style law to co-draft an acceptance standard. Prototype a Word and Google Docs add-in plus a records-system-neutral upload, pilot it with 2 small departments already testing AI report tools, and offer public defenders an 'AI-report discovery audit' service.

title: Receipts-Only Reviews via Open Banking
one_liner: Reviews that only people who provably paid can post, with the payment verified through open-banking data and only merchant, amount band and month disclosed.
customer: UK and EU independent restaurants, salons, tradespeople and clinics (verified-review widget and profile subscription), with lenders, insurers and marketplaces as later data buyers.
problem: Trustpilot removed 4.5M fake reviews in 2024 and was fined by Italy in Mar 2026 for failing to verify authenticity. The FTC rule and UK consumer law ban fake reviews, and no platform can verify offline purchases. Merchants cannot prove their reviews are real, and review sites sell services to the businesses they rate.
solution: The reviewer links a bank through an open-banking account-information partner (such as TrueLayer or GoCardless). The app reads one transaction and produces a selective-disclosure attestation (merchant, amount band, month), then posts. Merchants get a '100% paid-customer reviews' widget and structured-data markup. Reviewers get neutral, sentiment-independent cashback funded by merchants.
why_now: Fake-review enforcement is intensifying (FTC warning letters Dec 2025, Italy's Trustpilot fine Mar 2026), the AI-generated review flood is growing, and AI shopping agents ingest reviews as trust signals. Open banking now has enough UK users to make linking a normal action.
revenue_model: GBP 19-49 per month merchant subscription, API and data licences to lenders and marketplaces, and float on cashback funding.
non_obvious_insight: The referee problem vanishes when the proof comes from the bank, not the platform. A review site that sells to the businesses it rates can never be trusted, but a receipt cannot be bought.
first_30_days: Sign 30 independent restaurants in one UK city, put a QR code at the till, and build on an open-banking partner's sandbox. Launch with local press as 'the review site you cannot buy'.

title: Water Towers as Virtual Power Plants
one_liner: Aggregate municipal pump stations and elevated tanks into a controllable flexible load that dodges peak-coincident charges and earns demand-response and capacity payments, with a hard guarantee on pressure and fire reserve and an operator veto.
customer: Cities and districts that pump water, especially cities that own both the electric and water departments (common in the Midwest, Texas and the Southeast) and utilities with transmission-level or large demand-charge accounts. The buyer is the utilities director or the city manager, with the finance director as the champion.
problem: Electricity is one of the largest controllable costs for a pumped water system. Yet most pumping schedules are simple level setpoints written years ago, and operators keep tanks fat out of habit and fear. The unspoken rule is that nobody ever got fired for a full tank. Meanwhile the grid has turned pumping hours into money. Peak-coincident charges such as 4CP in ERCOT and peak load contribution tags in PJM are set by just a handful of hours per year. Capacity prices have spiked in recent auctions. Big load additions are pushing retail rates up. Water utilities are physically able to shift a large share of pumping, but no vendor is selling it to the 10-100k-population systems in a form an operator trusts.
solution: A small edge box or cloud service that reads tank levels, pump status and pressure from SCADA (OPC-UA or Modbus, read-only at first). It computes safe curtailment windows per station with hard constraints: fire and emergency reserve never touched, minimum pressure kept, projected demand over the event covered, water-age limits respected. It pre-cools tanks before predicted grid peaks and auto-releases if any constraint is threatened. Operators see one screen and can veto or end an event in one tap. Phase one is pure peak-coincident avoidance and time-of-use shifting, which needs no market enrollment. Phase two enrolls the stations as a curtailment resource through a demand-response aggregator partner or directly.
why_now: Recent PJM capacity auctions cleared at or near the price cap, on the order of $100k or more per curtailable megawatt per year before an aggregator's cut. Data center load growth is pushing capacity and transmission costs into retail rates, and RTOs and utilities are expanding demand-response programs. Edge controllers and OPC-UA gateways are cheap, and small teams can now build reliable forecasting for tank levels and peak intervals. (Auction figures are from memory. Verify current prices before pitching.)
revenue_model: 25-40% of verified savings and demand-response revenue, with no upfront cost to the utility and a small monthly platform fee. Utilities with both electric and water departments can be sold a bundled controls contract.
non_obvious_insight: The constraint is not physical but psychological and legal: operators are (rightly) terrified of a pressure or fire-flow failure. The winning product is not optimization software but a guarantee with a veto. Sell the operator the ability to stop it at any moment and the CFO the savings. Also, water and electric are often the same city, and the city has never put both budgets on one page.
first_30_days: Target three small cities that own both electric and water in ERCOT or PJM territory and have published tariffs. Get read-only SCADA access at one pump station, or historical CSV exports of tank levels and pump runs. Replay a year of the data to show what a 4CP or PLC avoidance schedule would have saved with reserves untouched. Bring that dollar figure to the city manager, and sign a shared-savings pilot on one pump station.

title: Settlement Back Office for Farm Water Conservation
one_liner: Program administration as a service that enrolls small farms in paid fallowing and conservation programs, verifies acre-feet with satellite evapotranspiration plus meter data, pays within 14 days, and hands the farm's CPA a clean tax packet.
customer: Payers: irrigation districts, state and basin conservation programs, corporate-funded coalitions and cities buying temporary leases, who pay the admin fee. End users: family farms of 50-800 irrigated acres in the Colorado River basin.
problem: The 2027-2036 framework pushes the next cuts onto agriculture, which takes about 70% of the river. Buyers want verified acre-feet at a price per acre-foot. Farmers want simple metering and fast payment, and fear that fallowing weakens their water right. Amazon's $20M ($32M raised toward a $100M goal) shows demand with no settlement layer. Programs run on spreadsheets and site visits, so small farms wait months and mis-report the income.
solution: A portal that enrolls farms and sets a consumptive-use baseline from public field-scale ET data, pump-power meter data and the farm's own records. Local crop advisors are paid per visit to verify. Contract templates carry a 'right-protection' letter agreed with the state water agency. ACH payment in 14 days. Automatic W-9 and 1099 handling, plus a tax and books packet on income timing and conservation-payment treatment for the farm's CPA. Funders get an audit-ready acre-foot ledger.
why_now: Interior issued the Record of Decision in Aug 2026 with Powell and Mead at about 36% of capacity. 95% of the basin is in drought. Corporate and public conservation money is arriving with no back office. Free satellite ET data and cheap power-meter telemetry now make remote verification credible, and LLMs make program-specific agreements and tax packets cheap.
revenue_model: 3-5% of disbursed funds as a program admin fee. $150 per farm onboarding fee, paid by the program. Later, a spread on instant-pay float. A $100M coalition goal at 4% is about $4M of admin revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Water markets fail at settlement and trust, not price discovery. A farmer will fallow if he is paid in weeks and his water right is legally shielded. The winning product is paperwork plus a legal shield letter plus a tax packet, not a marketplace. The customer who pays is the funder who would otherwise have to staff a program office.
first_30_days: Approach 3 irrigation districts or NGOs running conservation pilots and offer to administer 20-40 farms for a flat pilot fee. Build the enrollment form, an ET baseline report from public data and ACH payout in 30 days. Sign an LOI with one coalition partner. Recruit an agricultural CPA and a water attorney as advisers to draft the shield-letter approach.

title: Publish the Obvious: Generative Prior Art vs. Patent Thickets
one_liner: Turn cheap AI generation into a defensive weapon by industrially publishing dated, enabling disclosures of every obvious variant around a product, so secondary 'evergreening' and troll patents can't be granted.
customer: Primary: generic and biosimilar manufacturers and public-interest funders (procurement agencies, health-access NGOs) facing secondary patent thickets on drugs losing primary protection. Secondary: hardware, robotics and protocol-foundation startups afraid of patent trolls.
problem: Secondary patents on dosing regimens, polymorphs, formulations, devices and manufacturing tweaks extend monopolies long after the core compound expires, and they are cheap to file, especially now that AI drafts applications. Challengers' tools (IPR, oppositions, litigation) are expensive and come after the patent issues. Startups have no defense budget against troll assertions.
solution: A pipeline in which LLMs plus a patent agent or PhD reviewer enumerate the design space around a target product: formulations, dose schedules, salt and crystal forms, delivery devices, process variations. It drafts enabling defensive disclosures and timestamps them. It deposits them where examiners actually search (IP.com Prior Art Database, Research Disclosure, plus DOI-bearing repositories such as Zenodo and ChemRxiv that patent-office non-patent-literature tools crawl). It then monitors new filings, maps which disclosures block which claims, and files third-party submissions where the law allows. Sold as a per-product 'novelty shield' with measurable outcomes: examiner citations and rejections.
why_now: Compound patents on semaglutide and other blockbuster GLP-1s are expiring in several large markets in 2026, triggering a stampede of generic entry and follow-on patent strategies. LLMs now make it cheap to enumerate enabling variants at scale. Patent offices are swamped and revising guidance on AI-assisted work, and nobody has industrialized the defensive side of the novelty game.
revenue_model: $15-80k per product-family shield for generics and funders; $500-2k/month subscriptions for startups and foundations; success-based bonuses when a filing is rejected citing a disclosure; grant and NGO funding for public-health targets.
non_obvious_insight: Prior-art status depends on what was publicly and enablingly disclosed, not on who or what wrote it. So when generating variations is free, the asymmetric weapon is to publish the space before anyone can claim it. The scarce thing is no longer ideas but credible, discoverable, dated publication. It also aligns the incentive: the parties who pay (generics, health funders) gain directly from the commons staying open.
first_30_days: Pick 3 products with visible secondary-patent thickets and imminent generic entry. Produce about 200 enabling disclosures per product, each reviewed by a contracted patent agent. Publish to two or three searchable indexes. Send free 'thicket map' reports to 5 generic makers and 2 access-focused funders. Sell the first shield for $15-25k. Track later filings to prove examiner citations. Have patent counsel vet the approach up front, including that every disclosure is actually enabling and accurate.

title: Junior Studio OS for Teen Game Developers
one_liner: Payroll, enforceable contracts, a custodial legal shell and payout splitting for teenage Roblox and Fortnite creator teams that already run large studios without knowing they are businesses.
customer: Teen (13-19) founders of UGC game studios and their parents, plus adult publishers, investors and acquirers who want to back teen studios safely.
problem: Roblox creators earned over $1.5B in 2025, and top studios are run by teens and early twenties. But minors can disaffirm contracts, collaborators across countries expect revenue splits, payouts land in personal or parent accounts, taxes are misunderstood, and there is no cap table. Disputes and co-founders who leave with the IP kill studios, and investors avoid them.
solution: A 'studio in a box': a custodial LLC or UTMA structure with guardian co-signature and court-approval flow for larger deals. A rev-share ledger reads DevEx and group payouts and splits them automatically. It collects W-9/W-8 forms and sets aside tax reserves. It provides a parent-co-signed, ratify-at-18 contract template with IP assignment and vesting, plus a diligence data room for acquirers.
why_now: Roblox creator payouts were over $1.5B in 2025 (about 70% year-over-year growth), the standard DevEx rate rose to $0.0038 per Robux in September 2025, and 2026 rate changes reward higher-spending audiences. Teen studios are hiring peers and getting publisher attention. Fortnite (UEFN) and Minecraft marketplaces add more teen earners.
revenue_model: SaaS of $19-$49 per month per studio plus 1-2% on managed payouts, a $500-$2,500 legal setup package, and diligence or introduction fees from publishers and investors.
non_obvious_insight: Their barrier is not creativity, it is legal personhood. When a 15-year-old's game earns $20k per month, the biggest risk is a co-founder who quits with the IP or a signature that is not binding. Selling enforceable trust wins the studio and later the deal flow, making the OS the accepted source of diligence on teen studios.
first_30_days: Join the top 50 Roblox developer Discords and the DevForum. Offer a free 'who owns what' studio audit to 30 teen studios. Sell a $299 done-for-you custodial entity plus rev-share agreement drafted by a youth-entertainment lawyer, and get 10 paying by day 30. Pitch three UGC publishers on sourcing through you.

title: Revocation List for Leaked ID Documents
one_liner: A neutral, hashed registry of compromised license and passport records that every verifier can check, forcing step-up on IDs from the Nexus/IDScan.net dump.
customer: IDV and KYC vendors, marketplaces, gig platforms, neobanks, telecom and car-rental retail, and lenders, buying an API.
problem: On Aug 31 2026 the Nexus market began selling 153M+ US and Canadian driver's licenses, each with six images including infrared and ultraviolet scans. Researchers call stored ID images 'permanent fraud tools'. Verifiers cannot tell a fresh scan from a leaked record, and issuers will not revoke tens of millions of licenses.
solution: Ingest breach corpora only through controlled, lawful channels (researcher and law-enforcement partners, hash-only contributions). Compute privacy-preserving fingerprints (salted hashes of document number, state and DOB combinations, and perceptual hashes of portraits). Expose an API answering 'has this document instance been seen compromised?' with a risk tier and recommended step-up (mobile ID, bank-account link, in-person). Add hash-prefix consumer lookup and DMV reissue guidance.
why_now: The Nexus dump is the biggest leak of ID scans and follows 2025 leaks of ID photos from age-verification and support systems (e.g., Discord's vendor). Document-image KYC now needs a compensating signal, and verifiers have none.
revenue_model: $0.01-0.05 per check or $2-20K per month subscriptions, with consumer-alert partnerships through banks.
non_obvious_insight: Public-key infrastructure solved 'a trusted key was stolen' with revocation lists, not by preventing theft. Issuers will not revoke documents, but verifiers can pool what they know. The leak itself is the data source, and the value comes from the shared list.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 breach researchers and one small IDV vendor. Build the hashing pipeline and API, and clear the design with privacy counsel. Give it free to 10 verifiers, then convert by usage.

title: Age Assurance Kit for Small Game Communities
one_liner: A drop-in age-gating kit that never stores IDs, with regulator-ready audit trails, for indie multiplayer studios, mod sites, fan forums and Minecraft-style server networks.
customer: Indie multiplayer studios (5-100 staff) with in-game chat, modding and fan-wiki sites, forums, and server networks selling ranks, mainly in the UK and EU.
problem: The UK Online Safety Act enforcement deadline was 2025-07-25, and Discord announced mandatory face-scan or ID checks worldwide in March 2026. Discord's Sept 2025 breach was claimed to have exposed 2.1M ID photos, and photo checks were beaten with Death Stranding character images. Small operators have mandates with no compliance budget.
solution: An SDK and plugin set (Unity, Unreal, Discord bot, Discourse, WordPress, Minecraft servers) that routes each user through the cheapest sufficient method (on-device estimation, card check, reusable wallet attestations). It stores only a signed over-13 or over-18 token, and ships risk-assessment templates and audit logs.
why_now: Enforcement is live, the Roblox and Discord rollouts set user expectations, and a leaked-ID breach makes 'we never hold your ID' a selling point.
revenue_model: $29-199 per month per community plus $0.02-0.10 per verification, with a documentation package for regulators.
non_obvious_insight: Large vendors sell to big platforms, but the long tail needs self-serve pricing and paperwork, not just a verification call. The liability is holding the ID, so a token-only design is the product, not a feature.
first_30_days: Ship a Discord bot and WordPress plugin on top of an existing estimation and wallet vendor. Recruit 20 forum and server operators through modding and Minecraft communities. Convert 5 to paid plans and write the regulator documentation pack.

title: Renewal Radar for Silent AI Exclusions
one_liner: Track carriers' filed AI exclusions and tell brokers, 90 days before renewal, which clients just lost AI coverage, then place the affirmative buy-back.
customer: Independent agencies and regional brokers (10-200 staff) with commercial books, their E&O carriers, and MGAs.
problem: Since January 2026 ISO-style generative-AI endorsements (CG 40 47 and CG 40 48) and far broader carrier forms, such as W. R. Berkley's 'absolute' AI exclusion, are attached at renewal, often buried. Clients use AI in ways they never disclosed. Brokers carry E&O exposure for failing to warn, and no tool maps which of a broker's 300 clients face AI exclusions or what AI each client actually uses.
solution: A rate and form filing scraper (public SERFF filing access) plus an endorsement parser that normalises exclusion breadth: gen-AI only versus any AI, bodily injury versus advertising injury, vendor-supplied AI. It feeds a renewal calendar imported from agency-management CSVs. A 12-question client AI-use questionnaire, optionally backed by an SSO or expense-report scan for AI tools. Output is a one-page 'AI coverage gap letter' plus a list of affirmative AI markets for placement.
why_now: 1 Jan 2027 renewals are the first big cycle after the Verisk endorsements became available, and AIG, Great American and Berkley filings landed through 2026. Affirmative AI capacity now exists (Armilla via Lloyd's, AIUC, Munich Re aiSure), so a gap and its fix can be sold together.
revenue_model: $250-800 per month per agency, $150-600 per gap letter for non-subscribers, 10-15% commission on affirmative cover placed, and $2-5k per month filing-intelligence subscriptions for MGAs and carriers.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is triggered by their own E&O fear, not curiosity about AI. The filings are public but unreadable, so the moat is a normalised exclusion database nobody at a brokerage has time to build. Silent AI cuts both ways: an unexcluded policy is a reason to ask for affirmative cover, so the gap letter also works as a sales tool for the broker.
first_30_days: Scrape SERFF filings in five large states and build the tracker. Start a free weekly 'AI exclusion tracker' newsletter aimed at 500 brokers. Offer 10 agencies a $500 concierge gap audit on their five biggest accounts. Sign one affirmative-AI MGA for placement referrals.

title: Consented Elder-Speech Data Co-op via Storytelling Clubs
one_liner: Senior-living oral-history clubs where residents opt in, get a life-story book and pay, and their de-identified speech is licensed under strict speech-recognition-only, no-cloning terms to voice-AI and ambient-scribe companies.
customer: Speech-AI, ambient clinical documentation, hearing-aid and companion-robot teams buying elder-speech training and test data (per audio hour). Senior-living operators host the clubs for engagement and a revenue share, and families receive the recordings.
problem: Voice and scribe AI is tuned on younger speech and underperforms on 80+ voices, hearing-aid users and dementia, Parkinson's or stroke speech. AI labs now need clean chain-of-title (Suno swapped to a licensed-data model on Sep 9), and older adults are adopting AI (23% of 65+) while distrusting how their data is used (69% of 50+ are uncomfortable sharing health records with AI). The people who could supply ethical data, and who deserve to be paid for it, have no rights infrastructure.
solution: Trained facilitators (retired teachers, social workers) run recorded storytelling sessions in senior-living communities. Every participant passes a capacity screen with a family or health-care-proxy co-signature and can withdraw. Each clip carries a machine-readable consent scope (recognition and understanding only, never voice synthesis or cloning), is de-identified, and is tracked in a rights ledger that supports revocation and audit. Residents receive cash, the community gets a share, and families get an edited memoir and audio archive.
why_now: Licensed-data pressure is peaking after music and text lawsuits, and the EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency rules began applying in Aug 2026. Voice AI is being pushed on seniors just as they adopt it, and the 80+ cohort is the fastest growing group in the country.
revenue_model: Buyers pay roughly $80-150 per audio hour under a per-dataset license. About 25-30% goes to participants, 15% to the host community, and the rest covers facilitators and platform costs. Family memoir and archive packages are a $149-299 upsell.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not more hours of speech. It is consented hours from the oldest speakers, and only eldercare operators can gather them ethically, because capacity screening, proxies and revocation are the whole product. The strictest license terms (recognition only, no cloning) are what let elders and families say yes.
first_30_days: Pilot in 3 communities with an ethics review from a local university IRB or elder-law adviser. Record about 40 hours and secure a letter of intent from 2 to 3 elder-focused voice or scribe teams for a 100-hour dataset. Use the memoir book as the participant-facing hook.

title: Dealer-Fee Decoder for Solar and Home Loans
one_liner: Use the auto F&I trick of hiding the buy-down in the price to expose the hidden 'dealer fee' inside 0% and low-rate solar, HVAC and roofing loans, then sell the evidence to consumer lawyers and the refinance to credit unions.
customer: First: consumer-protection and TILA law firms and legal aid running home-improvement and solar loan cases, at $49 to $149 per decoded loan. Second: credit unions and community banks that pay $150 to $300 per funded takeout loan.
problem: A '0% for 12 months' or '2.99% for 20 years' home-improvement loan is not cheap. The lender charges the contractor a discount or 'dealer fee' that commonly runs into double digits on promotional-rate loans, and the contractor recovers it by inflating the price for financed customers. It's the same mechanic as a dealer's reserve and buy-down in an auto F&I office. The borrower sees a low APR, cannot see the cash price they should have been quoted, and often pays a financed price 15 to 30% above the cash price. Minnesota's attorney general has sued GoodLeap over hidden fees folded into loan amounts, and complaints keep growing. Homeowners left with orphaned systems and no tax credit are a sympathetic and litigable group.
solution: A document-parsing decoder. The homeowner or lawyer uploads the contract, TILA disclosure and any competing cash quote. The tool extracts price, APR, term and any disclosed fee, and estimates the implied cash price and implied finance charge, meaning how much of the price is really interest. It compares this to a regional cash-price benchmark built from scraped quotes, contractor bid sites and permit data. It outputs a plain-language one-pager and a lawyer-grade exhibit for TILA and UDAP claims, then offers a credit-union takeout quote for the true payoff amount.
why_now: The federal residential solar tax credit for homeowner purchases ended after 2025, a wave of installers went bankrupt and left homeowners with loans on systems nobody services, state attorneys general have started suing, and the CFPB's federal enforcement has faded so states and private plaintiffs are the enforcement. Contingency-fee plaintiff firms are already advertising for GoodLeap-type cases and need faster intake screening.
revenue_model: Per-case fee from law firms ($49 to $149), a subscription for high-volume firms ($499 per month), and a bounty from credit unions for each funded refinance or takeout loan. Later, a compliance benchmark sold to honest contractors, to lenders and to regulators.
non_obvious_insight: Consumer advocates attack solar lenders as if the fee were unique to solar. A finance manager knows it is standard structure anywhere a merchant can 'buy down' a rate: the retail price quietly carries the cost. What law firms lack is not the theory but cheap, defensible, per-loan numbers to screen thousands of leads. The cash price counterfactual is the missing piece and the F&I mindset is exactly what tells you where to look for it.
first_30_days: Collect 200 real solar and HVAC loan document sets and cash-vs-financed quote pairs from public complaints, forums and two or three law-firm partners. Build the parser and implied-price model on them. Offer three plaintiff firms with active solar-loan intake 25 free screens each, then charge $99 a case. Meet two credit unions with home-improvement loan programs to agree a bounty for takeouts.

title: Launch Kits for the First Psilocybin Clinics
one_liner: A readiness and operations service that helps ketamine and TMS clinics and state-licensed psilocybin centers get staffed, compliant and billable before the first FDA approval.
customer: Interventional psychiatry clinics (ketamine, TMS, Spravato sites) and state-licensed psilocybin service centers in Oregon and Colorado, paying $8-20k for a readiness audit plus $3-6k a month for ops software.
problem: Trend chain: Compass's COMP360 has positive phase 3 data and a new CEO (Sep 2026) for a 'coming launch', so an approval is plausible within about a year (timing uncertain). Then treatment needs 6-8 hour monitored dosing sessions with trained monitors, recovery rooms, screening, integration follow-up and prior authorization. Then the sites have four times the chair-time of Spravato, no proven billing model, and some Oregon centers have already closed for lack of economics.
solution: Phase 1: a readiness audit covering space design, staffing model, screening protocol, day-long-session P&L, and payer mix, plus monitor training through partners. Phase 2: ops software for scheduling day-long sessions, pooling monitors across clinics, integration follow-up, REMS-style reporting and prior-auth packets.
why_now: Compass is preparing filing and launch. Oregon's program is live and Colorado opened licensed healing centers in 2025, so a paying pilot audience exists today. The 2024 FDA rejection of Lykos's MDMA showed how much process rigor matters. Ketamine clinics are consolidating and want a new line.
revenue_model: Readiness audit fee, monthly ops subscription, training seat fees, and a margin on a shared monitor staffing pool.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for the first psychedelic drug is chair-hours, not efficacy: 6-8 staffed hours per treatment with no settled reimbursement. The team that builds the day-long-session P&L and staffing model first owns the picks-and-shovels position.
first_30_days: Interview 20 ketamine and TMS clinic owners and 5 Oregon or Colorado center owners. Publish a free 'psilocybin chair-hour P&L calculator' to capture leads. Sell three readiness audits at $8-10k.

title: Rent Renewal Desk for Small Tenants
one_liner: Contingency-fee lease-renewal negotiation for tenants under 5,000 square feet, armed with the comps and lease abstraction that landlords get from CoStar-class data and small tenants never see.
customer: Independent restaurants, salons, clinics, small offices and shops with leases expiring in 6 to 18 months. Channels: bookkeepers and CPAs, POS providers and merchant associations.
problem: Landlords and their brokers negotiate with professional comps and lease abstracts, while small tenants negotiate blind. Tenant-rep brokers skip small deals because the commission is too small, so owners accept the renewal escalator, the personal guarantee and CAM charges by default. Crowdsourced comp platforms such as CompStak sell to brokers and investors, not to a florist with a lease renewal.
solution: The tenant uploads the lease and the last 12 months of CAM invoices. The desk builds a comp set (public deeds, listing asking rents, pooled tenant-contributed leases, licensed broker data), then returns a one-page 'you pay X% over or under market' report plus a negotiation script and draft letter. An optional we-negotiate tier uses a licensed broker partner, and a CAM audit is an upsell. Renewal alerts fire 18 months before expiry.
why_now: LLM document extraction can now abstract a 60-page lease and CAM reconciliation in minutes at a cost of cents, work that used to cost a lawyer $500 to $1,500. Tariff and wage pressure has made rent the last fixed cost small operators can still attack. CompStak's give-to-get model shows lease data can be crowdsourced when contributors get something back.
revenue_model: A $149 fair-rent report. 20% to 25% of first-year rent savings for full negotiation. 25% contingency on CAM overcharges recovered. Bookkeeper and association referral revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: Information asymmetry is total at the small end, and the professionals who could close it are priced out by deal size. AI cuts the cost of a competent negotiation to a few hours. The lasting moat is a pooled, tenant-owned lease database, because landlords' data is proprietary but tenants' data is scattered and freely contributed if they get their own comps back.
first_30_days: Offer a free fair-rent check to 50 businesses in one dense commercial corridor through two local bookkeepers and a merchants' association. Build the lease-abstraction pipeline and a first comp set from the leases collected. Close five contingency negotiations, measure realized savings, and use the results as the sales deck for the next 100 tenants.

title: Alcohol Bridge: GLP-1 Addiction Care for Hospitals
one_liner: A hospital-embedded service that starts naltrexone plus semaglutide at discharge for alcohol use disorder with PEth monitoring.
customer: Hospital addiction-consult teams and liver clinics, plus health plans and employers paying for alcohol-related admissions.
problem: Only ~2% of people with alcohol use disorder get medication. A Lancet RCT (May 2026, n=108) showed semaglutide cut heavy drinking days in AUD with obesity, with NNT ~4.3 vs 7+ for approved drugs, and NIH-reported work shows added benefit on top of CBT. Phase 3 trials and the VA's CRAVE trial are running, but clinicians have no protocol, and opioid bridge clinics got settlement money while alcohol, the bigger killer, got none.
solution: A bridge service at discharge: naltrexone alone or with semaglutide (per trial eligibility, BMI 30 or more), PEth blood monitoring every 4 weeks, telehealth follow-ups and a cash-pay pill pathway, with outcome reporting on readmissions and PEth negatives.
why_now: The first RCT and NIH coverage landed in 2026, GLP-1s are now cheap and familiar, and hospitals are under margin pressure from readmissions. Off-label use requires careful protocols, so first movers will set the standard.
revenue_model: $250-400 per patient per month billed to hospitals, payers or employers, plus grant and state SUD funds where eligible.
non_obvious_insight: Alcohol-related admissions repeat and cost the hospital, but no service line owns the medication step. The wedge is a discharge protocol, not a new clinic.
first_30_days: Approach 3 hospital addiction-consult teams and hepatology clinics. Recruit an addiction-boarded medical director and run a 30-patient quality-improvement pilot under the hospital's existing governance, charging a ~$20k pilot fee.

title: Convert Empty Thai Hotel Floors to Monthly Stays
one_liner: Take under-filled floors of mid-tier Thai hotels on revenue share and run them as furnished 30-90 day remote-worker wings, replacing lost Chinese group demand with sticky monthly stays.
customer: Owners of 80-300 room three- and four-star hotels in Bangkok, Phuket, Pattaya and Chiang Mai whose Chinese group volume collapsed. End users are remote workers, retirees and long-stay sports or wellness visitors.
problem: Thailand's 2025 arrivals fell 7.2% and sit 17% below 2019, with Chinese arrivals down 33.5%. Insiders wait for Chinese groups to return, but Chinese outbound is shifting to independent travellers who go farther and spend less on hotels. Empty floors bleed fixed costs, while nomads on 40+ visa schemes struggle to find reliable monthly stays.
solution: We take 20-40% of rooms and add a coworking corner, bonded fast internet, laundry, community events and monthly billing. Guests pay USD 650-1,100 per month including utilities, for a 30-day minimum. We market through nomad communities and groups and help with long-stay visa paperwork. The hotel keeps F&B upside.
why_now: The China demand collapse leaves stranded capacity. Thailand's long-stay Destination Thailand Visa exists for remote workers, and 40+ countries now offer nomad visas. Nomad information is now free (Nomads.com sells lifetime membership for USD 1), so operators win on product, not discovery.
revenue_model: A 20-30% management fee on room revenue or a fixed lease spread, plus ancillary revenue from SIMs, insurance and visa-service referrals.
non_obvious_insight: Hotels are optimised for nights while nomads buy months. A floor at 90% occupancy on monthly rates beats 35% occupancy at full nightly rates, and monthly guests do not pay 22-28% OTA commission.
first_30_days: Sign 2 hotels in Bangkok or Chiang Mai on a 60-day trial of 10 rooms each. Build a one-page site and post in nomad and expat groups. Target 15 monthly bookings, and record occupancy and revenue per available room against the hotel's nightly baseline.

title: Timed Slots for Viral Fields and Harvest Rescue
one_liner: Ticketing built around bloom and ripeness windows that turns crop-trampling influencers and crew-short fields into capped, paid visitor days.
customer: Specialty and mid-size growers with photogenic or U-pick crops near metros (tulips, lavender, sunflowers, blueberries, peaches, apples, pumpkins), especially those with unharvested acres from crew shortages. Rural tourism boards are a second payer.
problem: Viral fields get trampled while farmers earn nothing, and destinations lack allocation tools (Fuji's hard cap is the model). Meanwhile fruit rotted in fields in 2025 for lack of pickers and late or absent H-2A crews mean lost revenue. Farms squeezed by diesel up 80% and a fourth loss-making row-crop year need any extra income.
solution: Bloom and ripeness forecasts from degree-day models and owner photos drive timed-entry capacity by field zone, waivers, weigh-station POS for pay-per-pound U-pick, and parking and shuttle management. A 'harvest rescue weekend' feature lets a farm that is short of pickers list a paid visitor-harvest event 5-10 days out, with dynamic pricing by forecast and weather. Dispersal nudges route overflow to lesser-known partner farms, and nearby motel beds can be bundled.
why_now: Crew shortages, high input costs and social-media virality are all at peak in 2026, and destinations from Barcelona to Glasgow are moving from fees to allocation. Agritourism liability laws are widespread. Lead times are shortening to about 33 days, so last-minute local trips are growing.
revenue_model: 8-12% of ticket value plus $1.50-$2.50 per ticket in payments. $199/season SaaS for farms. Sponsored dispersal campaigns from tourism boards.
non_obvious_insight: A crop calendar is a supply curve with a 7-14 day peak, so the same forecast tells a farmer when to harvest and a tourist when to come. One dataset prices both the labour gap and the crowd, and U-pick as an emergency labour substitute is a hedge farms already improvise but nobody productises.
first_30_days: Sign 5 orchards and pumpkin farms for immediate October weekend slots to test capacity caps and pricing this month. Then sign 10 farms for spring 2027 tulips and strawberries starting in January, using white-label Stripe ticket pages before building custom software.

title: Drone-Checked Eruv Boundaries
one_liner: Scheduled autonomous drone inspection of the utility-wire boundaries that define an eruv, so communities learn before Shabbat whether a line is down.
customer: Eruv committees and synagogues in the US and abroad (hundreds of communities), plus Jewish federations and city-level committees.
problem: An eruv's boundary is often miles of utility wire, checked weekly by volunteers on foot or by car. A break invalidates carrying on Shabbat, and storms and tree limbs cause breaks. Utilities do not notify committees.
solution: Weekly autonomous flights (drone-in-a-box under Part 107 first, then BVLOS), computer-vision detection of wire discontinuity and pole damage, and GPS-pinned photo alerts to the committee. The rabbinic authority stays the decision-maker, and the tool provides the time-stamped evidence.
why_now: The FAA's Part 108 BVLOS rule cleared to OIRA (final review) in July 2026 and was not yet published as of mid-September. Drone docks and vision models are cheap. A 2016 proposal in Israel showed interest but no commercial product surfaced.
revenue_model: $300-1,500/month per eruv plus a setup fee, then adjacent inspection contracts (cemetery and campus perimeters, congregation roofs and steeples).
non_obvious_insight: The religious need is verification, not construction. A weekly audit trail with time-stamped imagery is exactly what a committee needs for its Friday declaration, which converts a religious-legal requirement into a recurring inspection budget line.
first_30_days: Contact 5 eruv committees (for example Baltimore, Teaneck, Cleveland). Fly VLOS segments with a Part 107 pilot, build a wire-break detection dataset, and sign 2 paid pilots at about $250/month.

title: Human Callback Line Sold Through Credit Unions
one_liner: A staffed 'is this really my grandson?' phone line and call-screening kit for members over 70, paid for per enrolled member by community credit unions whose deposits walk out the door in voice-clone scams.
customer: Community banks and credit unions with $300M-$5B in assets and an older membership, paying about $3-6 per enrolled member per month. A secondary direct-to-family tier is $12 per month paid by adult children.
problem: Voice cloning needs only a few seconds of audio, and older adults are losing large sums to family-emergency and impersonation scams. The FBI reportedly counted about $352M in AI-linked fraud losses among people over 60 in 2025, and the FTC estimates most fraud goes unreported. Victims are shamed and rushed, and the scam's whole design is to prevent a pause. Most transfers are authorized, so banks are usually not liable, but the member's savings leave the institution and often end up in a crypto ATM.
solution: A screen-free service: one memorable number on a fridge magnet and phone sticker. Whenever anyone calls asking for money or urgency, the member hangs up and calls the line. A trained human (retired tellers, 911 dispatchers, nurses) runs a slow 5-minute out-of-band check: pre-registered family safe word, a call-back to the real relative through their stored circle, and a plain-language 'this matches a known scam script' verdict. Members with large cash withdrawals or wires get a teller prompt that says 'want to call the line first?', with the credit union's flag visible to the desk. Enrollment happens at branches and senior centers with a 20-minute family safe-word ritual.
why_now: Voice-clone scams have moved from novelty to mainstream in 2025-26. Regulators, state elder-exploitation reporting duties and the UK's mandatory reimbursement rules for authorized push-payment fraud point the direction US institutions are heading. Credit unions are competing on trust and member service against fintech, and have no good product for the fraud they cannot block.
revenue_model: B2B2C per-enrolled-member fee ($3-6 per month) with a pilot flat fee of about $2,000 per month per credit union; overage for call volume; $12 per month direct-to-family plan; optional add-on to sell to insurers of members' homes and autos.
non_obvious_insight: Against a perfect fake voice, the only durable defense is a slow, human, out-of-band ritual, and the buyer is not the senior but the institution holding the money. The scam is a deposit-flight event, and credit unions have the branch relationship, field-of-membership community ties and senior-center access to reach victims before the scammer does. Making the 'moment of doubt' land on a number people already trust is cheaper than any AI detector.
first_30_days: Pitch one sub-$1B credit union through its CEO or member-experience lead (reach them via state credit union league events and CUNA meetups). Recruit 8 retired tellers and dispatchers to staff phone shifts from home using Twilio and a shared inbox, with no engineering needed. Enroll 60 seniors from a local senior center in a 60-day pilot and log every attempted scam reported. Sell the results as a member-perk pilot at $2,000 per month.

title: App-Diet Service for the Phone-Upgrade Freeze
one_liner: As phones get unaffordable, today's handset becomes a five-year handset, so old-device performance decides who keeps users.
customer: Banks, wallets, telcos and government digital services with large user bases on 2-3GB RAM Android phones in Africa, India and LatAm.
problem: Memory-driven price rises are stretching replacement cycles. Bloated apps crash on old devices, and churn from that is invisible in analytics.
solution: A fixed-price audit on a real farm of used 2GB phones on 2G/3G. Deliver sub-10MB lite builds and WhatsApp or USSD fallbacks, then a monthly regression retainer. The wedge is a four-week audit for one mid-tier bank or wallet.
why_now: Memory is 30-40% of phone cost, LatAm shipments fell 10%, and GSMA's $40 phone pilot shows the price problem.
revenue_model: $15-40k per audit and $5-10k per month for device-lab monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone forecasts the next phone. The second-order effect is that the current phone lasts far longer, so performance on old hardware, not features, drives retention.
first_30_days: Buy 15 used phones and publish a teardown of the top 10 fintech apps in Nigeria or India. Use it to book audits.
